{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0.0) or shows early signs of bearishness.",
    "Reduce forecast peaks after sharp spikes — model tends to overreact and overshoots in the short term.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5-10% to align with historical volatility.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, cap upward revisions after 3 consecutive days of rising prices to avoid overconfidence.",
    "If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.33), maintain forecast but slightly dampen volatility by reducing standard deviation of forecast range.",
    "When true outcome is below 65.00, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for downward momentum.",
    "If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a downward correction of 5–10% to avoid overestimation."
  ]
}
